app.stateError: Could not read the launcher's state: {{error}}

jobs.gameStopped: The game stopped (exit code {{code}}). See Log.

library.title: Your arcade
library.description: Add the folders of the games you own. The launcher recompiles each one on this computer from your own files, to play here or to export for Android and RetroArch.
library.pickFolder: Choose a game folder (the one holding game.exe)
library.emptyText: Choose a game's folder: the one with its game.exe. The launcher recognises the supported games by their executable.

status.title: Status
status.missing: The folder is gone or no longer holds this game. Point the launcher at it again below.
status.ready: Recompiled for this computer and ready to play.
status.stale: Built from another copy of the game or by an older launcher: build it again.
status.none: Not recompiled yet. Building takes a minute or two and uses only your own copy of the game.

game.noPlayer: Playing here is not available on this computer yet
game.noPlayerText: There is no x2-player for this system. You can still export the game for Android or RetroArch.
game.removeText: Forgets this folder and deletes what was built from it. The game's own files are not touched.

display.title: Display
display.vsyncText: Present in step with the display. Off, the game paces itself at its own 60 Hz.
display.fpsText: Starts with the frame-rate overlay on.
display.scaleText: The game's frame rendered at a multiple of its size. Automatic picks the largest that fits 1280×1024.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.envText: Extra runtime switches, one KEY=VALUE per line (see Debugging → Switches in the docs).

controls.title: Controls
controls.description: Which controller button presses each of the cabinet's buttons. The keyboard works too (see Controls in the docs).
controls.layoutText: A starting point; change single buttons below.
controls.pressButton: Press a button on your controller…
controls.fixed: Start, Back (coin; hold for the test menu) and the d-pad keep their roles.

layouts.stickKof: 8-button stick (L1 / L2 rows): A C over B D

export.title: Build for another platform
export.description: Recompile your games into a RetroArch core or the Android app. Everything is built here, from your own files; copy the result to your device.
export.neededSome: {{tools}}. Some must be installed separately (see Build tools).
export.noGames: Add games in the Library first.

androidRetroarch.name: RetroArch core for Android
androidRetroarch.description: typex2_libretro_android.so with the chosen games. Copy it to RetroArch/downloads/ on the device, then Load Core → Install or Restore a Core.

androidApp.name: Android app
androidApp.description: typex2.apk: the standalone app (ES-DE can launch it) with the chosen games. Needs the Android SDK's build tools next to the NDK.

hostRetroarch.name: RetroArch core for this computer
hostRetroarch.description: The libretro core for RetroArch on this computer, with the chosen games. Copy it and typex2_libretro.info into RetroArch's cores folder.

tools.title: What building needs
tools.description: The launcher downloads its compilers into its own folder: nothing is installed on your computer, and Remove takes it all away. Tools you already have are used when nothing was downloaded.

use.compile: Compiling games to play on this computer

hints.kit: Part of this app. In a checkout: {{command}}
hints.ccMac: Or install Apple's Command Line Tools: xcode-select --install
hints.ccLinux: Install clang from your distribution's packages

tools.jobsText: Compilers running at once. 0 uses every core but two, so the computer stays responsive.
tools.ndkText: Only when an NDK you installed yourself is not found by itself.

log.title: Output
log.gameEmpty: The game's output appears here while it runs.

about.description: Static recompilation of Taito Type X and Type X2 arcade games: each game's x86 code is translated to C and compiled to native code, with Windows, Direct3D, DirectSound and the JVS I/O board provided by the runtime.
about.yoursText: The launcher, the recompiler and the runtime contain no game code or data. Games are recompiled on your computer from your own copies; what is built stays in the launcher's folder and in the exports you make.
